The dominant signal is Phase I xenobiotic metabolism: methimazole (CHEBI:50673) and biphenyl-4-amine (CHEBI:1784, the metabolic surrogate of N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl) converge on Reactome Phase I - Functionalization of compounds (REACT:R-HSA-211945, FDR=5.14e-4) and its child pathway Biological oxidations (REACT:R-HSA-211859, FDR=7.09e-4). Biphenyl-4-amine alone maps to the CYP1A2-mediated aromatic amine N-hydroxylation pathway (REACT:R-HSA-211957, FDR=1.88e-3), while methimazole maps to FMO oxidises nucleophiles (REACT:R-HSA-217271, FDR=1.88e-3), reflecting its known flavin-monooxygenase inhibition pharmacology. The second axis is selenium-dependent biology: the selenium atom (CHEBI:27568) is the sole hit in three WikiPathways entries — Pluripotent stem cell differentiation pathway (WP:WP2848, FDR=1.88e-3), Ferroptosis (WP:WP4313, FDR=4.27e-3), and Selenium micronutrient network (WP:WP15, FDR=7.27e-3) — all driven by the selenium-dependency of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and selenoprotein expression. The third axis is arachidonate-derived eicosanoid signalling: mummichog's m/z-direct network analysis ranked Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate (MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate, p=0.0074) as the top hit, with the thromboxane A2 KEGG:C02198 and six structurally related prostaglandin/thromboxane metabolites forming a tight network cluster. Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) appeared at rank 8 with p=0.0195. Benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (KEGG:C14853, CHEBI:30614) — a DNA-adduct-forming PAH diol epoxide — reinforces the xenobiotic exposure theme. D-Glucose (KEGG:C00221) and beta-mercaptoethanol (KEGG:C00928) showed network adjacency to glycolysis and glutathione pathways but did not reach significance independently. react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm enrichment of 8 differentially abundant metabolites reveals three biologically coherent axes. The dominant signal is Phase I xenobiotic metabolism: methimazole (CHEBI:50673) and biphenyl-4-amine (CHEBI:1784, the metabolic surrogate of N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl) converge on Reactome Phase I - Functionalization of compounds (REACT:R-HSA-211945, FDR=5.14e-4) and its child pathway Biological oxidations (REACT:R-HSA-211859, FDR=7.09e-4). Biphenyl-4-amine alone maps to the CYP1A2-mediated aromatic amine N-hydroxylation pathway (REACT:R-HSA-211957, FDR=1.88e-3), while methimazole maps to FMO oxidises nucleophiles (REACT:R-HSA-217271, FDR=1.88e-3), reflecting its known flavin-monooxygenase inhibition pharmacology. The second axis is selenium-dependent biology: the selenium atom (CHEBI:27568) is the sole hit in three WikiPathways entries — Pluripotent stem cell differentiation pathway (WP:WP2848, FDR=1.88e-3), Ferroptosis (WP:WP4313, FDR=4.27e-3), and Selenium micronutrient network (WP:WP15, FDR=7.27e-3) — all driven by the selenium-dependency of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and selenoprotein expression. The third axis is arachidonate-derived eicosanoid signalling: mummichog's m/z-direct network analysis ranked Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate (MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate, p=0.0074) as the top hit, with the thromboxane A2 KEGG:C02198 and six structurally related prostaglandin/thromboxane metabolites forming a tight network cluster. Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) appeared at rank 8 with p=0.0195. Benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (KEGG:C14853, CHEBI:30614) — a DNA-adduct-forming PAH diol epoxide — reinforces the xenobiotic exposure theme. D-Glucose (KEGG:C00221) and beta-mercaptoethanol (KEGG:C00928) showed network adjacency to glycolysis and glutathione pathways but did not reach significance independently. No structural conflicts were found between KEGG and ChEBI representations of the PAH diol epoxide; the thromboxane annotation showed connectivity-level heterogeneity between the KEGG and ChEBI namespaces, consistent with isoform diversity.

RaMP-DB ORA identified three selenium-anchored WikiPathways: Selenium micronutrient network (WP:WP15) ranks first among selenium pathways with FDR 0.00205, followed by Pluripotent stem cell differentiation pathway (WP:WP2848) at FDR 0.000722 and Ferroptosis (WP:WP4313) at FDR 0.00111. The selenium atom (KEGG:C01529, ChEBI:27568, InChIKey BUGBHKTXTAQXES-UHFFFAOYSA-N) is the sole overlapping metabolite across all three RaMP hits. Simultaneously, mummichog m/z-direct analysis places prostaglandin formation from arachidonate (MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate) as the top-ranked pathway by p-value 0.00496, with 3 overlapping metabolites that include thromboxane A2. final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm enrichment of 8 differentially abundant metabolites reveals three biologically coherent axes. The dominant signal is Phase I xenobiotic metabolism: methimazole (CHEBI:50673) and biphenyl-4-amine (CHEBI:1784, the metabolic surrogate of N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl) converge on Reactome Phase I - Functionalization of compounds (REACT:R-HSA-211945, FDR=5.14e-4) and its child pathway Biological oxidations (REACT:R-HSA-211859, FDR=7.09e-4). Biphenyl-4-amine alone maps to the CYP1A2-mediated aromatic amine N-hydroxylation pathway (REACT:R-HSA-211957, FDR=1.88e-3), while methimazole maps to FMO oxidises nucleophiles (REACT:R-HSA-217271, FDR=1.88e-3), reflecting its known flavin-monooxygenase inhibition pharmacology. The second axis is selenium-dependent biology: the selenium atom (CHEBI:27568) is the sole hit in three WikiPathways entries — Pluripotent stem cell differentiation pathway (WP:WP2848, FDR=1.88e-3), Ferroptosis (WP:WP4313, FDR=4.27e-3), and Selenium micronutrient network (WP:WP15, FDR=7.27e-3) — all driven by the selenium-dependency of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and selenoprotein expression. The third axis is arachidonate-derived eicosanoid signalling: mummichog's m/z-direct network analysis ranked Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate (MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate, p=0.0074) as the top hit, with the thromboxane A2 KEGG:C02198 and six structurally related prostaglandin/thromboxane metabolites forming a tight network cluster. Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) appeared at rank 8 with p=0.0195. Benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (KEGG:C14853, CHEBI:30614) — a DNA-adduct-forming PAH diol epoxide — reinforces the xenobiotic exposure theme. D-Glucose (KEGG:C00221) and beta-mercaptoethanol (KEGG:C00928) showed network adjacency to glycolysis and glutathione pathways but did not reach significance independently. No structural conflicts were found between KEGG and ChEBI representations of the PAH diol epoxide; the thromboxane annotation showed connectivity-level heterogeneity between the KEGG and ChEBI namespaces, consistent with isoform diversity.
